pages.quiz:
GERMAN — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #8
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: GERMAN
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. German for “school” is: (1 mark)
   A. Wasser
   B. Haus
   C. Schule
   D. Buch

2. When practising Active Listening, Interactive speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening, Interactive speaking.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening, Interactive speaking.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Active Listening, Interactive speaking.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening, Interactive speaking.

3. When practising Listening for information, Oral Expression, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening for information, Oral Expression.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for information, Oral Expression.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening for information, Oral Expression.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for information, Oral Expression.

4. “Guten Tag” means: (1 mark)
   A. Good day / hello
   B. Thank you
   C. Good night
   D. Please

5. When practising Active Listening Interactive speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening Interactive speaking.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening Interactive speaking.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Active Listening Interactive speaking.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening Interactive speaking.

6. When practising Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Extensive Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Extensive Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Extensive Reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Extensive Reading.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
7. In three clear sentences, explain Listening for information, Oral Expression and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

8. In three clear sentences, explain Active Listening, Interactive speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

9. In three clear sentences, explain Extensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

10. In three clear sentences, explain Speed Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Schule

2. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening, Interactive speaking.

3. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for information, Oral Expression.

4. A — Good day / hello

5. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening Interactive speaking.

6. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Extensive Reading.

7. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening for information, Oral Expression; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

8. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Active Listening, Interactive speaking; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

9. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Extensive Reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

10. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Speed Reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
